title: Walmart to Begin Accepting Apple Pay in U.S. Stores
content:
After years of holding out, Walmart today announced that it will finally begin accepting tap-to-pay options like Apple Pay in some of its Walmart and Sam's Club stores in the U.S. starting Monday, August 24. The retailer plans to roll out tap-to-pay support to all of its U.S. stores by the end of 2026 and to its gas stations by mid-2027.


"We want customers and members to have choice in how they pay, so they can check out in the way that works best for them," said Walmart, in a press release. 

Other major U.S. retailers like The Home Depot, Lowe's, Kroger, and Texas-based grocery store chain H-E-B already reversed course and rolled out tap-to-pay support in recent years, leaving Walmart as one of the most notable remaining holdouts until now.

Before this, Walmart prioritized its own Walmart Pay system that involves scanning a QR code at checkout, but it has finally listened to customer feedback and decided to accept NFC-based tap-to-pay options like Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Samsung Pay at its U.S. stores. Tap-to-pay support extends to physical credit and debit cards.

With Apple Pay, launched in 2014, you can simply hold your iPhone or Apple Watch near the payment terminal to pay with a digital version of an eligible credit or debit card stored in the Apple Wallet app. Apple Pay has a lot of privacy protections, including hiding a customer's actual credit card number during the payment process.

Existing payment options like Walmart Pay will remain available.

title: Apple TV isn’t worth the wait
content:
Macworld





A few weeks back, this site (and indeed this reporter) excitedly covered the news that Severance was back, baby. A cryptic tweet from showrunner Ben Stiller indicated that third-season shooting had begun, in the first bit of good news for fans since the brilliant second season ended on March 20 last year.
But is the show really back? The problem is that shooting and post-production take a lot of time. Even if everything goes perfectly to plan, we’re looking at a third-season launch in fall 2027 at the absolute earliest, more than two and a half years after the second one arrived. For comparison, the first five seasons of The Sopranos were released across a span of 1,883 days; at that point, we’ll still be months short of Stiller’s team releasing their third, and with fewer episodes per season (13 each for The Sopranos vs 9 and 10, respectively, for the first two seasons of Severance). And even a show as superb as Severance simply isn’t worth that kind of wait.
The joy of TV is its connectedness, the way it allows you to follow a story across multiple instalments as the narrative builds and breathes. Your experience of one episode informs your response to the next. Your memories of earlier seasons make the events in later seasons matter.
Think about the bombshells that landed in later seasons of Game of Thrones (eight seasons across nine calendar years), and how much less we would care about those characters and their fates if we hadn’t lived through dozens of previous episodes alongside them. Think about the montage sequence at the end of The Wire (five seasons across seven years) and how much its emotional force depends on everything that’s come before. And then think about how difficult it was to even remember what was going on when you sat down to watch Severance season 2 more than a thousand days after the first season finished.
There were reasons for that gap. The Covid pandemic, which had delayed the first season, was still a factor while filming the second. There were also actors’ and writers’ strikes to contend with. On top of that, the show wasn’t officially renewed for a second season until a couple of days before the first finished airing, so perhaps the team wasn’t sure where they stood or ready to get started right away. It was never going to be an easy job turning around another season for the following year. But surely the third season ought to have been less of a challenge, given the absence of Covid and the show’s obvious status as an Apple flagship.
Severance is returning… at some point.
Ben Stiller / X




It might seem unfair to compare Severance, a streaming hit of the 2020s, with the prestige cable dramas of the 2000s and 2010s. So let’s focus on other Apple properties.
Pluribus dropped its brilliant first season in November 2025 and was promptly renewed for a second, but essentially nothing has been heard since. When questioned this month, creator Vince Gilligan sighed heavily and said it was going to be a long time. Late 2027 seems optimistic; 2028 may be more realistic. Dark Matter wrapped up its first season on June 26, 2024, and is returning for its second season on August 28. The Morning Show, one of the only original Apple TV+ shows, is on an almost perfect two-year cadence. Even sitcom Ted Lasso, which wrapped up season 3 on May 31, 2023, only just kicked off its fourth season a couple of weeks ago.
In the case of Pluribus, as Gilligan explained, the show is a challenge from both a narrative and a logistical point of view. That’s almost certainly true of Dark Matter. And Ted Lasso wrapped up its original story in season 3, so a longer delay is understandable. But taking your time isn’t free. It costs something, particularly when you’re part of the zeitgeist. Pluribus was embedded in the culture, and the culture has moved on. Memes have a short memory.
Now consider Slow Horses, whose return for a sixth season was officially announced this month. That show is almost the polar opposite of Severance, having achieved a phenomenal rate of more than one season per year. And this pays off. The characters remain in the viewer’s mind between seasons–and when one returns, as in the new trailer, it can be played as a shocking reveal. You don’t need a lengthy recap when referring to the twists and turns of previous seasons. I don’t think the writing of Slow Horses is anywhere near as complex as that of Severance, but the show as a whole works better because it maintains a solid release rate.
Ben Stiller, if he stumbled across this article, would probably retort that the superior qualities of his show are a direct result of taking more time over each season (and that Slow Horses has the advantage of adapting a series of books). I couldn’t entirely disagree with that, although there’s plenty of evidence to show you can make a classic TV show within time constraints and without direct source material. Look at ER, which made one season a year, like clockwork, for 15 years. Look at its spiritual successor, The Pitt, which has happily dropped into the same pattern. It can be done without compromising on quality.
Granted, there is something very appealing about saying to creators, “Please, take your time, and make it as close to perfect as you possibly can. There’s no rush.” I absolutely get the beauty of that idea. But the reality is that at some level, beyond a certain point, there is always a rush: If you wait too long, even the most loyal of viewers will forget and move on. Apple TV deserves better than that.

title: Smartphone Sales Are Falling Worldwide, But Apple Keeps Growing
content:
Apple gained ground in India, Latin America, and Europe even as all three markets contracted, according to a new series of Counterpoint Research reports.


Between late March and the beginning of August, Indian smartphone sales ran 14% behind the equivalent stretch of 2025, and the market slipped for three straight weeks once major promotions in July had finished. Apple outperformed every rival with a 15% rise, which Counterpoint attributes to strong iPhone 17 demand holding up alongside continued affordability offers. Samsung and OPPO each grew just 4% in the country.

The research firm added that promotions are borrowing demand from the weeks either side of them, rather than growing the market. Amid broad price rises, Counterpoint expects the Indian smartphone market to finish 2026 down around 13%.

Latin American smartphone shipments fell 10% in the second quarter, which is the region's steepest annual drop since the third quarter of 2023. Apple and Samsung were the only brands to grow, by 5% and 6% respectively, while Motorola, HONOR, and Xiaomi all receded in the market. Apple's gains apparently came from absorbing component cost increases rather than passing them on to customers, and the company now accounts for roughly 51% of everything sold above $600 in the region.

European shipments dropped 10% to 35 million units, which is the weakest second quarter in three years. Apple added nine percentage points of market share to achieve parity with Samsung, with each now on 34%, and Xiaomi on 15%. No other brands sit above 4%. Counterpoint expects further declines as inventory dries up, but forecasts that Apple will continue outperforming the wider market.

smartphone market in China was down 8.6% across the first 30 weeks of the year, with the rate of decline widening back into double digits once the popular 618 shopping festival had concluded. Apple's sales have slowed since July, with discounts pulled back across retail channels and much of the summer's demand already spent during promotions. Counterpoint expects that lull to last until the new iPhone lineup arrives. Huawei, meanwhile, led the market throughout in the region, holding more than a fifth of weekly sales since April.

title: When to reuse, sell or recycle an old iPhone or iPad
content:
An old iPhone or iPad may have years of useful life left, but the wrong second act can turn aging software into a security risk. Here's how to tell when it deserves a new job, a new owner, or a trip to the recycler.

Apple devices can be repurposed
Most retired devices still have a working display, usable cameras and enough battery life for undemanding tasks. A clever project can keep that hardware out of a drawer, but novelty alone doesn't make the project worthwhile.
Repurposing an old device can save money and postpone another purchase, but a second life isn't automatically useful or responsible.
Using an iPad solely as an e-reader can provide real value with limited security exposure. An iPhone that no longer receives security updates shouldn't stay signed into messages, banking apps, saved passwords, or smart-home controls.

title: I’ve seen the new iPhone 18 Pro colors. This is one to get
content:
Macworld





When it comes to rumors about a new iPhone, some people are interested in specs—cameras, chips, AI features, etc.—but everyone wants to know what new colors it will come in. Now that we know, after my sources revealed to Macworld the likely color options for the iPhone 18 Pro lineup earlier this year, you’re probably wondering: What’s the best color option this year?
Every year, Apple introduces at least one new iPhone color that becomes a signature for that generation. Last year it was Cosmic Orange, a surprisingly bold choice that helped the iPhone 17 Pro stand out from its predecessors. This year, according to information we’ve heard from sources, Apple plans to replace the vibrant orange with something a bit more sophisticated.
Rumored iPhone 18 Pro colors
The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max are expected to come in four colors this year. The star will be a new shade of dark red reportedly called “Dark Cherry,” in addition to more conventional options such as silver and dark gray. And although Apple’s plans may change, those considering upgrading their iPhone this fall are already thinking about which color to choose.
Based on what we know so far, here’s a breakdown of the rumored colors for the iPhone 18 Pro, and which one we think will look best.
Silver: The safe choice

Foundry




Every new iPhone needs a classic color that never goes out of style, and silver has been fulfilling that role for years. Silver is expected to be among the color options for the iPhone 18 Pro, and to be honest, it’s probably one of the best choices for those planning to keep the same phone for years.
Fun colors are nice, but you might eventually get tired of them. Silver is timeless, elegant, and it also goes perfectly with other Apple products that aren’t available in fun colors (such as the MacBook Pro). I chose silver for my iPhone 17 Pro Max last year, and I haven’t regretted it.
Also, rumors suggest that this year’s iPhone models will feature a silver-toned glass back instead of pure white, giving the rear a more seamless look.
Dark Gray: The color for pros

Foundry




Nothing says “pro” quite like black or dark gray devices. And although Apple had offered black iPhones for years, that option simply disappeared with last year’s iPhone 17 Pro.
However, according to our report, Apple has considered bringing back a darker color option for this year’s iPhones. The color would be a Dark Gray rather than pure black, but it would undeniably be a big hit among those who want something more subtle and sleek. The last time Apple made a gray iPhone Pro was the Graphite iPhone 13 Pro, which is one of our favorites of all time.
Apple was rumored to be developing a “Steel Gray” iPhone 17 Pro last year, but that option never made the cut. So, we’re hoping it makes the cut for the final production this year.
Light Blue: For a little whimsy

Foundry




The rumored light blue color option for the iPhone 18 Pro is certainly one of the biggest surprises. The only time an iPhone Pro model offered a color like this was in 2021 with the Sierra Blue iPhone 13 Pro. It’s still one of my favorites to this day.
However, our sources say that this year’s blue finish is much softer than recent blue options such as Pacific Blue or Deep Blue. If you’re tired of gray phones but don’t want something as distinctive as Cosmic Orange, Light Blue might quietly become the sleeper hit of the lineup.
If you’re a fan of blue like I am, this option is the one for you. Sierra Blue is one of the most elegant iPhone colors ever made, and if this new Light Blue is anything close, it’ll be an instant classic.
Dark Cherry: The one that screams ‘new iPhone’

Foundry




Just as Cosmic Orange makes the iPhone 17 Pro instantly recognizable, Dark Cherry will do the same for this year’s iPhone 18 Pro models.
Beginning earlier this year, iPhone 18 Pro rumors began pointing to a “deep red” color as a follow-up to Cosmic Orange. But based on information from Macworld sources, the new color will skew closer to a deep wine, purplish hue than the bright red of sports cars. And that makes a lot of sense for an iPhone Pro.
A true red iPhone Pro would have taken the iPhone Pro line in an aggressive direction following Cosmic Orange. Dark Cherry, on the other hand, is a return to the Pro line’s sophistication. It’s bold enough to feel different, but restrained enough that it still feels unmistakably like a Pro device.
Since publishing our original report, we’ve also seen real-world evidence pointing to this finish, which only reinforces our confidence that Dark Cherry will be the signature color this year. If Apple gets the metallic finish right, Dark Cherry could become one of those colors people immediately associate with a specific iPhone generation, much like Cosmic Orange or Deep Purple before it. 
Since the iPhone 18 Pro isn’t expected to look much different from the current generation, Dark Cherry is the finish to choose if you want an iPhone that looks brand new.
Apple knows iPhone colors matter
While tech specs are important, there are many customers who also spend a lot of time thinking about which iPhone color they should choose. That’s why Apple invests so much effort into developing signature finishes. A distinctive new color makes an upgrade feel immediately recognizable, even before you notice faster performance or better cameras.
This year’s color lineup feels more restrained than the iPhone 17 Pro’s, yet it’s shaping up to be one of the most diverse in years. Instead of leaning on a bold color, Apple appears to be embracing a more mature palette centered around darker, richer tones. For some buyers, Silver or Dark Gray will always be the right choice. Others will appreciate how different Light Blue looks compared to previous Pro iPhones.
But if someone asked me today which finish best captures what the iPhone 18 Pro generation is supposed to represent, I’d point to Dark Cherry without hesitation. While Cosmic Orange was something of a wild card, Dark Cherry is a signature iPhone Pro color and will surely be its best seller.
Of course, color is entirely subjective, and that’s exactly why Apple offers multiple options. But if you’re the kind of buyer who upgrades every few years and wants your new iPhone to actually look new, I’d skip the safe choices this time. Dark Cherry appears to be the finish that best captures this generation, and the one people will remember long after next year’s iPhone arrives.

title: You don’t need a new Mac. You need a new keyboard
content:
Macworld





How much time do you spend in front of your Mac every day? If it’s more than an hour or two, there’s one upgrade you can make that will transform your experience in an instant: a mechanical keyboard. This simple change can step up your productivity and make typing the most comfortable it’s ever been.
Take it from me. I’ve been using and reviewing Mac-friendly mechanical keyboards for years. I’d never go back to Apple’s Magic Keyboard, never mind any of the thousands of cheap and nasty rubber-dome alternatives that flood the market.
It really is something you have to feel to understand. Once you do, you’ll never look back. The mechanical hype is real. Here’s why you should make the switch.
Pure typing bliss
As the name suggests, a mechanical keyboard is defined by the mechanical switches that lie underneath its keycaps. Each time you press a key, it moves downward on a spring-loaded mechanism, sends a signal to macOS, then moves back up.
Conversely, on a standard keyboard such as Apple’s Magic Keyboard, the keycap sits atop a rubber dome. As you push the key, it moves downward onto the dome, which squishes down and actuates the key press.
There are several problems with this rubber dome system. The first is durability. The soft dome wears down over time, reducing the consistency of its interaction with the keyboard’s contact points and potentially introducing errors in your typing. The longer you use it, the less dependable it becomes.
Keychron Q6 Max
$239.99 at Keychron							
						
A mechanical switch, on the other hand, is made from much more solid metal or plastic that is designed to last. Some mechanical keyboards go a step further and use magnetic connections (based on Hall effect or tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) tech) to actuate each key press, reducing the number of physical contact points and increasing durability exponentially.
In other words, mechanical keyboards tend to be far more reliable in the long term, meaning fewer frustrating mistakes and costly replacements.
The second issue with rubber dome keyboards–the most important one–is the typing feel. Mechanical switches come in all sorts of shapes and sizes, from those that feature a tactile bump as you press the key to those that are entirely smooth in action. That’s important, because the switch you choose can have a big impact on the typing feel.
As someone who types all day, every day, I love a tactile switch because it provides physical feedback that helps me type with greater speed and accuracy than a non-mechanical keyboard ever could. For my use case, the difference between a tactile switch and a linear one–never mind a rubber dome keyboard–is night and day.
Many mechanical keyboards let you swap out the switches on the fly, giving you many different typing experiences that can be customized to your needs. You’ll never get that with a rubber dome keyboard, where you have to stick with its (often unsatisfying) under-finger feel through thick and thin.
A new world to explore
Mechanical keyboards have benefits. But aren’t they just for PC gamers? And what about the price? They’re all eye-wateringly expensive, right?
SM1 Slim Mechanical Backlit Bluetooth Keyboard
$99.99 at B&H											 | 
																		$99.99 at Best Buy US											 | 
																		$99.99 at Satechi							
						
I used to think that mechanical keyboards were just for Windows users whose idea of tasteful computer design was a blinding array of garish neon lights. But while that’s the stereotype, it’s far from the truth.
These days, many manufacturers are making Mac-specific mechanical keyboards. There are excellent offerings from the likes of Logitech, Keychron, NuPhy, Satechi, and more. Lofree has a superb range of Mac keyboards color-matched to the MacBook Neo, while Corsair even collaborated directly with Apple to create the K65 Plus, which is often on sale for under $120 and well worth the price.
These devices all use macOS key layouts. For example, the Option key is in the proper place, which isn’t the case if you use a keyboard designed for Windows. No adaptation or adjustment is needed. And with high-quality materials and beautiful designs that fit in with your Apple setup, these keyboards are far from the obnoxious gamer aesthetic.
Take the Keychron Q3 Max, for example, which is the mechanical keyboard I’m using right now to type up this article. It comes with macOS keycaps and a switch to toggle between macOS and Windows layouts (so the Option key is in the right place, which isn’t the case if you use a keyboard designed for Windows). Its all-metal case is rock solid; it looks downright gorgeous and sounds pleasing to the ear, and I can change its switches to a different type if I want a fresh typing feel. My fingers have never felt so luxuriated.

The Keychron Q3 Max is my current Mac keyboard and it’s a huge improvement over what Apple sells.

Foundry




All of the devices made by the companies I mentioned above use macOS key layouts, meaning there’s no adaptation or adjustment needed. And with high-quality materials and beautiful designs that fit in with your Apple kit, these boards are about as far from the obnoxious gamer aesthetic as it’s possible to be.
As for the price, sure, mechanical keyboards are often pricey, but so is the Magic Keyboard. And as Apple fans are well aware, expensive doesn’t equate to overpriced. You can easily find a mechanical keyboard that far exceeds the Magic Keyboard for the same price or less.
There are mechanical keyboards that push the price into $200 (or more), but in most cases you’re making an investment in quality. And if you don’t want to spend that much, you don’t have to. Even high-end brands such as Keychron sell entry-level mechanical keyboards starting at around $60.
Touch ID
The only advantage of an Apple keyboard is the Touch ID button. Due to the way Touch ID works, you won’t find a third-party keyboard with it. But this is much less of an issue than it might appear. If you have an Apple Watch, you can log into macOS and confirm purchases using it, just as you would with a Touch ID button. In fact, logging in is actually faster using an Apple Watch than the Touch ID button because it happens automatically.

An Apple Watch can make up for the lack of Touch ID on third-party keyboards.

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




If you don’t have an Apple Watch, you’ll have to enter your password to log in and at the checkout. On the plus side, the latter can be sped up considerably if you have a password manager that autofills your login details.
I have an Apple Watch, so I don’t miss the Touch ID button at all. But even if I didn’t, I wouldn’t trade it for a mechanical keyboard. The benefits far outweigh what you miss out on.
With a far superior typing feel, a huge range of switch options, plus exquisite quality and ingenious features everywhere you look, every Mac user can benefit from ditching the Magic Keyboard and exploring the world of mechanical alternatives. I made the leap years ago and have never regretted it. Perhaps you should give it a try and take a look at Macworld’s picks for the best keyboards.

title: Camera AirPods Code Reveals Image Capture Resolution, Status Light, Person Detection, and More
content:
Apple is working on camera-equipped AirPods, as indicated by various reports and a demo video of them in action discovered earlier this week. The video was found by MacRumors in the macOS Tahoe 26.7 release candidate, but it turns out there are even more details in the code.


MacRumors forum member mactracker has discovered a hidden macOS framework called "AccessorySensorManager" that manages sensor data from the AirPods when they are connected to a Mac. That's turned up the following information:


AirPods designed to capture paired color images: Code indicates the left and right earbuds have individual camera sensors that return synchronised RGB still images of up to 1 megapixel with matching frame IDs, giving Visual Intelligence the same scene from two angles. This doesn't rule out other sensors like infrared cameras, but they aren't mentioned in the code.


AirPods support periodic image capture but not video: The cameras take internal still frames for Visual Intelligence to process, rather than "taking pictures" or recording video. In "active" mode, the framework can request a synced pair of images, or it can receive a capture rate, where pairs of stills are continually sent at the specified rate.


Active and passive capture modes use different resolutions: In "active" mode, likely triggered by the user via Siri, the AirPods capture a 640x640 image and return a processed 1024x1024 image. "That's about 0.4 megapixels of sampled image data, and a little over 1 megapixel for the output frame," mactracker explains. In "passive" mode, they capture a 320x320 image that can return a 320×320 or 512×512 output. "These are capture-specific resolutions, and the physical sensor's native resolution may be larger," adds mactracker.


Passive mode appears intended for background environmental awareness: The framework mentions contextual conditions like nearby speech, changes in the surrounding audio, posture changes, head rotation, and movement outside a defined area. It's not clear from the code whether every condition triggers a camera capture.


AirPods account for continual head movement: The framework includes lens distortion correction, dual-camera calibration, and camera-to-motion sensor calibration. It can also reject images affected by excessive movement or an occluded view.


Some processing happens directly on AirPods: The code mentions "peripheral inference," or on-device detection of whether a person is in view.


Each AirPod likely has a capture indicator light: The framework contains code that allows it to remotely control a hardware indicator and its brightness, suggesting the AirPods have a light to let other people know when they are capturing still images.


Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has said that Apple no longer plans to release this model, and instead is working on a new generation of AirPods with cameras, codenamed B798. This makes it likely that the discovered framework is related to the canceled model. It also underlines that the findings show how Apple's camera-equipped AirPods could work, rather than a guarantee of the final product's features.

title: Apple smart glasses: Everything you need to know
content:
Macworld





According to reports, Apple is going to expand its presence in the wearable market with a new product: smart glasses.
The Apple smart glasses that have been reported are a departure from the spatial computing platform of the Apple Vision Pro. They won’t be a headset and they won’t offer AR or spatial computing. They aren’t going to be a computing device in any way. 
Instead, they will be glasses like those from Meta AI and other companies. They will be designed like typical eyeglasses, not a headset or goggles. They will have built-in cameras, speakers, and microphones for taking pictures and video, and to interact with the iPhone. These glasses are expected to function as an AI-powered wearable, potentially launching in 2027. 
This article will track the latest reports on the Apple smart glasses. Check this space often for the latest news before they are released.


Apple smart glasses design: What will Apple smart glasses look like?
Unlike the bulky Vision Pro, Apple’s smart glasses are expected to resemble a normal pair of eyewear.
Apple is said to be prioritizing a lightweight, accessory-like design rather than the heavy, immersive approach of the Vision Pro. To appeal to a mainstream audience, the glasses are rumored to be significantly lighter and more affordable, positioned primarily as an iPhone companion.
According to various reports, the glasses will look like traditional frames and will not adopt a headset-style design.
To accommodate the necessary hardware, the frames may be slightly bulkier than standard glasses and will likely use plastic or similar lightweight materials.
One potential frame style could be inspired by the glasses worn by Apple CEO Tim Cook.

One of the frame style coule be modeled after a pair of Tim Cook’s glasses.

Apple




Frame styles in development
In April 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple has four frame styles in testing:
A large rectangular frame, reminiscent of Ray-Ban Wayfarers
Larger oval or circular frames
A slimmer rectangular design, similar to the glasses worn by Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook
A smaller, more refined oval or circular option
Apple is also experimenting with finishes such as black, light brown, and ocean blue. The frames are reportedly made from acetate, which Gurman describes as “more durable and luxurious than standard plastic.”
Apple’s design approach
Apple is developing the frames in-house rather than partnering with third-party brands, unlike Meta (Ray-Ban, Oakley) or Google (Warby Parker). The goal is to create a product that is instantly recognizable as an Apple device.
Earlier reports suggest Apple is aiming for a higher level of build quality compared to competing smart glasses from Meta and Google.


						

							


Apple smart glasses features: What will Apple smart glasses do?
Apple’s smart glasses are expected to be a lightweight, AI-first accessory designed to complement the iPhone rather than replace it. Unlike the Vision Pro, which focuses on immersive spatial computing, these glasses will likely take a more subtle approach – similar to Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses – prioritizing everyday utility and privacy.
The glasses are not expected to function as a standalone device. Instead, they will rely heavily on a paired iPhone via Bluetooth. How much functionality will be available without an iPhone remains unclear.
The Apple smart glasses are reported to offer the following features:
Camera for video/photos: Users will be able to capture photos and record video directly from the glasses.
Visual Intelligence: The onboard camera will analyze objects and scenes in real time, enabling features like object recognition and contextual awareness.
Speakers: Built-in speakers will deliver audio from the iPhone, including calls, music, podcasts, navigation directions, and alerts.
Microphone: Used for phone calls, voice commands, and features like live translation.
Advanced Siri integration: A more capable, AI-driven Siri is expected to power most interactions and tasks.
Fixed heads up display: Likely limited to simple overlays such as notifications and turn-by-turn directions rather than full AR visuals.
Privacy focus: Apple is expected to emphasize on-device processing and secure cloud infrastructure to minimize data collection.
The built-in cameras are rumored to feature vertically oriented oval lenses with surrounding indicator lights, distinguishing them from the circular cameras used in Meta’s glasses.
Role in Apple’s ecosystem
One of the primary purposes of the smart glasses is to act as a wearable interface for Apple Intelligence. Much of their functionality will depend on Apple’s next-generation Siri, which is rumored to be previewed alongside broader AI upgrades at WWDC26. 

The Apple smart glasses could have health tracking features, but will not be as robust as an Apple Watch.

Apple




Advanced capabilities (rumored)
The first generation will likely focus on audio features and basic visual overlays. Over time, Apple is expected to evolve the product into true augmented reality glasses capable of rendering 3D digital content seamlessly within the user’s physical environment.
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple is exploring more advanced features, including:
Text recognition and digitization
Context-aware reminders (e.g., prompting you to pick up an item you’re looking at in a store)
More natural navigation guidance, with Siri referencing real-world landmarks instead of generic directions
Health tracking has also been mentioned, though it’s expected to be less comprehensive than what’s offered by the Apple Watch.


						

							


What specs are rumoured for the Apple smart glasses?
According to Mark Gurman, the device will likely use a modified version of the Apple Watch S-series chip. Apple is reportedly developing custom chips for the glasses based on the Apple Watch S-series, modified for extreme power efficiency to manage camera controls and AI tasks. 
The glasses are expected to include open-ear speakers, a microphone for voice commands, and a built-in camera for capturing photos and video. 
Reports indicate that Apple may chose a display-less design for its first iteration, similar to the Meta Ray-Ban glasses. 


						

							


Will Apple smart glasses support prescription lenses and different sizes?
The early reports for the Apple smart glasses have not stated if they can be outfitted with prescription lenses. Since other smart glasses support this, it seems likely that Apple will, too.
Reports have also not stated how Apple will handle frame sizing for customers. As prescription glasses wearers know, some frame styles fit better than others. Also, some styles can’t be used with multifocal lenses.
With the Apple Vision Pro, customers book demos at the Apple Store to get the experience of using one and also get fitted properly. Apple has this infrastructure in place and can use it with the new smart glasses.


						

							


Apple smart glasses name: What will Apple’s glasses be called?
No reports have been made regarding the name for the Apple smart glasses. Within Apple, the device has the code name of N50.
We can speculate on what the naming system will be, based on recent history. Apple no longer gives products “i” names, so it’s unlikely that they will be called iGlasses (though that won’t stop the media and others from calling it that until the official name is released).
“Apple” is in the company’s branding: Apple TV, Apple Vision Pro, Apple Business, Apple Music, Apple Podcasts, etc. So it seems like a viable possibility that this device will be called “Apple [something].”
This leads to whether Apple uses some form of the term “glasses” in the name. It seems unlikely that Apple will use “smart glasses.”
One interesting development to watch for is whether Apple decides to include the device in the Vision Pro lineup. If it does, then it will use some form of “Vision” in its name. If not, then Apple will not use “Vision” in the name in order to signify the separation.


						

							


Apple smart glasses release date: When could Apple smart glasses be released?
While Apple has made no announcements relating to smart glasses, it does seem that development work has been ongoing at the company for some time. Back in November 2024, Gurman reported that Apple had begun research into the smart glasses market by performing focus group discussions with Apple employees. Then, about a year later in October 2025, Gurman reported that Apple had decided to abandon its work on an Apple Vision Pro redesign to prioritize smart glasses.
Several detailed roadmaps from industry analysts suggest a launch could occur between late 2026 and 2028. 
Late 2026 Launch: Back in 2025 Mark Gurman suggested that Apple has big plans to release smart glasses in the second half of 2026. This is looking less likely now. 
2026 Preview with 2027 Launch: Apple might previewing this new category early, as it has done in the past: showing off the new glasses as early as 2026 as a preview, although the actual launch will be delayed until 2027. This was suggested by Gurman in December 2025. 
Launch in 2027: In February 2026, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that Apple made “significant progress” in the development of the glasses, and it could be ready for production by the end of the year, with a public release in early 2027.
Launch in 2028: Development delays relating to Apple’s AI could push the launch in to 2028. 
In August, the macOS 26.7 release candidate contained references to new products, including a possible update to the Vision Pro. Many of the references are unidentified model numbers, so one or several of these numbers may refer to the Apple smart glasses.


						

							


Apple smart glasses price: How much could Apple smart glasses cost?
No reports have been made so far regarding the prices for the Apple smart glasses.
For reference, here are the starting prices for the Meta AI glasses without prescription lenses and other lens options:
Ray-Ban Wayfarer (Gen 1) and Skylar (Gen 1): $299
Ray-Ban Wayfarer (Gen 2), Skylar (Gen 2), and Headliner (Gen 2): $379
Ray-Ban Blayzer Optics (Gen 2) and Scriber Optics (Gen 2): $499
Oakley Meta HSTN: $399
Oakley Meta Vanguard: $499
Apple will want to be competitive with these prices, but the variance is wide, so the company could offer the higher prices that you’ll often find with designer frames.

title: Best places to sell or trade in an iPhone in 2026: How to get the most money
content:
Macworld





In case you haven’t heard, there’s a new iPhone coming at Apple’s September event and that means two things: You want a new iPhone and you need to sell your old one. If you buy your iPhone outright every year or so, you can usually recoup a good amount of the new cost by selling your old model every time you upgrade to a new one. With prices for components so high these days, the trade-in prices have actually risen!
Even if you’re in the Apple’s Upgrade Program, you might have an older iPhone languishing in a drawer somewhere unused. Here’s what you need to know about selling or trading in your old iPhone for top dollar.
How to sell your iPhone online
Step one is deciding where you are going to sell your iPhone. You should start your research at third-party buyback sites. You’ll get an idea of what your phone in its current condition is worth, and then can either take that offer or try to directly sell your phone to another person yourself on Craigslist or eBay. You might want to mention you’re selling your phone on social media like Twitter, Facebook, or Instagram first, to see if a friend or associate wants it—you’ll feel better dealing with someone you know.
Buyback sites almost never give you as much money as a direct sale to another person would, but they’re much safer and easier. Sometimes the hassle of a direct sale to another person isn’t worth a little extra money, and you just want to quickly, easily, and safely get a reasonable price for your old phone. That’s where these sites come in. There are lots of buyback sites, but these are some of the biggest and most highly recommended: 
BackMarket 
BackMarket buys and sells used iPhones and other products. You can get up to $600 for an iPhone 16 Pro Max 512GB unlocked in Good (not even Flawless) condition, for example. A prepaid shipping label is provided so you can ship your iPhone off to them within 21 days of your quote. The quote is dependent on the iPhone matching the description you have given.
If you are in the U.K. BackMarket will also offer you money for your used iPhone. In this case, an iPhone 16 Pro Max 512GB unlocked in good condition but a few scratches could get you £340.
Compare and Recycle 
This trade-in service that assesses the different recyclers to offer you the best price on offer if you trade-in your iPhone. A search on Compare and Recycle suggested a 1TB, unlocked iPhone 15 Pro Max could be worth $571 with TheWhizCells.
The same search on Compare and Recycle in the U.K. suggested an iPhone 15 Pro Max could be worth £456 with Trade Your Phone.
Music Magpie
In the U.K. Music Magpie will buy used equipment from you (they were acquired by AO.com in 2024). Here our Good-condition iPhone 16 Pro Max 512GB unlocked could make us £594. You can lock in that price for up to 28 days. If you want to sell you just print out your free label. Once they get the phone and inspect it to make sure it’s in the condition you stated, they pay you the following day. If the condition is not as described, they will make a new offer. If that offer isn’t acceptable, they will return the phone free of charge.
Music Magpie used to trade as Decluttr in the U.S. but that site closed when the U.K. arm was bought.
Dennis Cortés/Unsplash
Gazelle
Gazelle buys and sells preowned smartphones, tablets, laptops, and other gadgets. They’ll give you an online quote for your item, and then send you a box to ship it to them for free. You can receive payment as a check, via PayPal, or in the form of an Amazon gift card.
The offer is good for 30 days, and Gazelle will make you a new offer if the item is in worse condition than you described. If you decide not to take the new offer, they’ll send your gadget back, but you pay for the return shipping. 
Swappa
Swappa works a little differently than most other buyback sites. It’s actually a marketplace where you sell directly to other customers—Swappa just verifies the listings, handles the payments (using PayPal), and organizes the shipping to reduce fraud. Swappa collects its fees from the buyer’s end, but the price the buyer actually sees has that fee as well as shipping included. The seller pays for shipping, and you’re on your own to package the item securely, too. 
Swappa lists a price range for what has sold recently on its site. You’ll sometimes be able to get more from a sale on Swappa, but selling directly to other people, even with Swappa’s protections in place, always assumes a little more risk. iPhone 15 Pro Max models have gone for around $605 here. 
Also read: Where to buy a second-hand or refurbished iPhone for more options where you might be able to sell it.
In the U.K. you can also sell your iPhone at places like CeX,  Envirofone, and We Buy Any Phone.
Trade in your iPhone for store credit
Another convenient approach is to turn in your old iPhone to the Apple Store, Amazon, Best Buy, or Walmart, where they’ll give you a gift card. You might not get quite as much, but these stores also take phones in worse condition than your typical buyer would expect. The big-box stores, for example, will give you a small gift card for an iPhone with a broken screen, while an Apple store will generally just recycle it for you. Sometimes these stores have preorder or launch-day deals as well, so keep your eyes open for that.
Apple
The Apple store’s online quote service is simple, fast, and generally offers pretty good prices for your used Apple gear. The downside is that you can only get an Apple gift card or credit toward the purchase of a new Apple product.
Apple offers trade-in values for all iPhones from the iPhone XR (up to $90) to the iPhone 16 Pro Max (up to $720). 
As of August 2026, Apple offers estimated trade-in values on the newer handsets: 


ModelEstimated trade-in value
iPhone 16 Pro Maxup to $720 / £680
iPhone 16 Proup to $630 / £600
iPhone 16 Plusup to $485 / £460
iPhone 16up to $480 / £445
iPhone 16eup to $310 / £345
iPhone 15 Pro Maxup to $530 / £480
iPhone 15 Proup to $420 / £435
iPhone 15 Plusup to $340 / £340
iPhone 15up to $335 / £325

 



We explain How Apple trade in works and saves you money separately.

Jason Cross/IDG




Amazon
Amazon Trade-In lets you sell certain products directly to Amazon in exchange for an Amazon gift card. It’s a very simple process, though it can take a couple of weeks before your item gets to Amazon and is inspected, so don’t expect a credit in your Amazon account immediately. The prices are often a little lower than other buyback sites, and you only get Amazon credit, but it’s very easy and safe.
Best Buy
Best Buy offers pretty good prices on trade-ins, and you can take your iPhone to a Best Buy location to drop it off, which might be more convenient than shipping it.
Walmart
Walmart contracts with CExchange to let you trade in smartphones, tablets, video games, and wearables for a Walmart gift card. You get a prepaid FedEx Ground shipping label, but you have to pack the item yourself. Then you get an eGift Card to spend at Walmart. 
In the U.K. stores like Argos, Currys and John Lewis will allow you to trade in an old iPhone.
Sell your iPhone back to your carrier
Not to be outdone, your carrier will accept trade-ins too. If you cringe at your phone bill each month, unloading old devices to your carrier might be tempting, since you can use the credit for new devices or to pay your bill. During the first couple months of an iPhone’s release, there may be special trade-in offers, so keep an eye out for that.
AT&T
For AT&T’s trade-in program, you can bring your device to an AT&T Store to get instant credit, or get a quote online and receive a kit to mail your device in for free. Then you’ll get a promotional card in the mail you can use to credit your bill or buy new stuff.
Verizon

Verizon lets you trade in devices with a prepaid shipping box. Credits can be applied to your bill, or you can opt for a gift card to use for new devices. 
T-Mobile

T-Mobile’s trade-in program is geared at people who want a new phone. Once you get a quoted price (for a phone in good condition), you’re taken to the store page to shop for a new device. You can also ship your phone or bring it to a T-Mobile store.
In the U.K. Carphone Warehouse will allow you to trade in an old iPhone, as will EE and Vodafone. However, U.K. based service Compare and Recycle warns that iPhone owners can lose out on £100s if they trade in with their phone network. 
Sell your phone directly to someone else
You can usually get the most money for your iPhone by selling it directly to someone else. Prepare your iPhone for sale, clean it, and take some good well-lit photos, then post it on eBay, Craigslist, OfferUp, or Facebook Marketplace (or all of the above). While this can be the most profitable route, it also could be the biggest headache and assumes the most risk. Scammers are everywhere! Follow these tips to help you sell your iPhone to someone else directly:
Only sell locally, never ship your iPhone to the buyer.
Only accept cash. Do not take a check, money order, Western Union, or any other form of payment. PayPal currently provides Seller Protection, but transactions need to qualify and you need proof — buyers can dispute the transaction and PayPal almost always sides with them.
Check out the buyer. Is this a one-off account with no other purchases or ratings? Do they have a social media presence? Are they trying to take the conversation off FaceBook or OfferUp to text messaging right away? These are all red flags!
Meet somewhere public and safe. Many police stations have “Safe Trade Zones” or “Internet Exchange Locations” specifically set up for buyers and sellers to meet. Banks are also a good option. Go inside, don’t handle your business out in the parking lot.
See and inspect the buyer’s money before you hand over your phone. Check for counterfeit bills or the old “stack of paper in a bank envelope” trick.
Which is the best option to choose?
If you want the easiest, most hassle-free experience and plan to buy another Apple product, Apple’s own trade-in program is a strong choice. 
The process is straightforward: you get a quote online, send in your device or bring it to an Apple Store, and receive credit toward a new purchase. 
Apple allows you to trade in multiple devices and the process is generally safe and reliable.
However, you typically won’t get the highest possible value. Apple’s trade-in values do fluctuate, but not always downwards: in May 2026, Apple raised maximum trade-in values on many devices and did the same again after raising prices for Macs and iPads in June. 
For the largest potential discounts on a new iPhone, especially when a new model launches, carrier trade-in deals are often unbeatable though. Carriers like AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon frequently offer up to $830–$1,000 off new iPhones with a qualifying trade-in and plan. For example, at launch Boost Mobile was offering $1,000 off the iPhone 16 lineup with its Infinite Access plan and a trade-in. The trade-off is that these deals come with significant commitments. 
How to get an old iPhone ready for sale
Now you have decided where to sell it you need to get your iPhone ready: wipe your data and make sure it is no longer associated with you before you pass it on to someone else. 
Apple has a list of what to do before you sell, give away, or trade in your old iPhone which is worth a look, and we also cover How to wipe and reset an iPhone. We recommend that you should check those guides out, but here’s our own advice for making sure you get the most value for a used iPhone:
1) Take good care of it
This probably goes without saying, but your iPhone’s condition plays a huge part in its value. So keep it in a case, use a screen protector, and generally try to keep it in great shape. If your phone shows some wear and tear, you’ll still be able to sell it, you’ll just get a little less money back. Also, holding onto the original box and including the charger (if it came with one) and cable also helps squeeze a little more value out of your sale.
2) Save your data
Before you get rid of your old iPhone, make sure all the data is backed up and ready to transfer to your new one. A backup to iCloud or the Finder (or the Music app if you are on a PC) is the most convenient way to sync all the data to your new iPhone, and another option is to sync directly from the old to the new iPhone. But because an iPhone backup is pretty self-contained, you may also want to separately make sure your photos are synced to Google Photos, iCloud Photos, or another cloud storage solution.

Michael Simon/IDG




3) Unpair your Apple Watch
If you have an Apple Watch, you should make sure it’s backed up,  unpair it from your old iPhone, and sync it with your new one. You can do this in the Watch app on the phone.
Tap the My Watch tab.
Tap All Watches at the top of the screen.
You’ll see all your Apple Watches paired to this iPhone.
Tap the (i) button next to your watch.
Tap Unpair Apple Watch.
If you have more than one Apple Watch paired to this iPhone, repeat this process for all of them.

IDG




4) Sign out of your Apple account
Sign out of your iCloud and Music accounts, too. This is a crucial step: If you erase your phone without signing out first, it will still have Activation Lock enabled and the buyer won’t be able to set it up! 
You should be prompted when you erase it (see below) but in case you’re not, here’s how to sign out: 
Head to the top of the Settings app. 
Tap your Apple ID and then scroll to the bottom of the next screen and tap Sign Out. 
You’ll probably be asked to confirm your Apple ID and password.

IDG




5) Reset your iPhone
Once you’re sure your iPhone is all backed up and ready to be fully erased, head to the Settings app and tap General > Transfer or Reset  iPhone (in earlier iOS versions the option says Reset). The nuclear option here is Erase All Content and Settings; if you’re selling or giving away your phone, this is what you want to do.
You may be prompted to turn off Find My iPhone and sign out of iCloud if you haven’t already—otherwise iOS’s Activation Lock will prevent the phone’s next owner from activating it. Confirm that you want to erase all the data, and your phone will be securely wiped and restored to factory settings. It’ll go through an update and you’ll be met with a “Hello” screen just like you were when you first set it up. Turn it off and say goodbye.
We cover this in more detail here: How to reset an iPhone. If you have any trouble you may find How to put an iPhone into recovery mode and return to factory settings useful. Note that you need to be connected to Wi-Fi or Cellular before you can wipe the iPhone.

title: How to put an iPhone into Recovery Mode if it’s not working
content:
Macworld





If you need to fix a faulty iPhone that will not start up properly, you can use Recovery mode. This lets you connect your iPhone to a Mac or PC and use it to update or restore iOS. If your iPhone is having problems, try updating the software first. This can reinstall iOS without wiping your data. If that does not solve the problem, you may need to restore the iPhone and start again.
If updating the software fails, you can use Recovery mode to restore your iPhone. Restoring wipes the device and installs the latest compatible public version of iOS. Once the restore is complete, you can set up the iPhone again and recover your settings, data, and apps from an iCloud or computer backup made before the problems started.
Recovery mode is also useful if you want to remove an iOS beta. This is not quite the same as wiping your iPhone to prepare it for sale – in that case, you should follow the normal erase process so that your data is removed and the iPhone is properly unlinked from your Apple Account.
Note: If you are considering Recovery mode because you have been unable to erase an iPhone using Erase All Content and Settings in Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone, first check that the iPhone has a working internet connection. That erase process may need to contact Apple’s servers, so make sure the device is connected to Wi-Fi or cellular data.
How to put your iPhone into Recovery mode

At a glance

Tools required: You will need the Finder on the Mac or the Apple Devices app on a PC to enter Recovery mode. Your Mac or PC will need to have a working internet connection. 

1.
Plug your iPhone into your computer using a cable that supports data


Foundry






You may see a message indicating that you need to unlock the iPhone to use the accessory – you can ignore this because you don’t need to unlock the iPhone to put it into Recovery mode. 

						

							
2.
Open the Finder (if you are on a PC it’s the Apple Devices app you need)

Finder on the Mac.

Foundry






If you were able to unlock the iPhone, you should see it in the Locations section in the right-hand column. If you don’t, don’t worry – the next step will put the iPhone into Recovery mode.

						

							
3.
Shut down your iPhone and enter Recovery mode
Keep holding the side button until you see this screen on your iPhone. 
Foundry






To shut down the iPhone you need to follow these steps: 
Press volume up
Press volume down
Press and hold the side button while the phone shuts down and starts up again – this means you must keep holding the side button even when it gives you the slider to turn the phone off and even when the Apple logo appears. 
Wait till the Recovery mode screen (shown above) is in place before releasing the side button.
Your iPhone is now in recovery mode.
To enter recovery on older iPhones the steps are slightly different: 
iPhone 7: Press and hold the Side button and Volume Down until the Recovery mode screen appears.
iPhone 6s and older: Press and hold the Home button and Side/Top button until the Recovery mode screen appears.
This should work even on an unresponsive iPhone, as long as it has enough power. If the iPhone is completely dead, connect it to power for a while, then try again.

						

							
4.
Update the software on your iPhone

Choose Update to update the software (and avoid wiping your iPhone)

Foundry






In the Finder click on iPhone, which should have appears under Locations on the right hand side.
You should now see a message indicating that there is a problem with the iPhone that requires it to be updated or restored.
Try the Update option first because that will update the software to the latest compatible version, without the need to wipe your iPhone. 
Updating the software may fix the issue you are having with your iPhone, but if that fails, you need to click on Restore. 

						

							
5.
Restore your iPhone (if the step above doesn’t work)

Restoring your iPhone will wipe it. 

Foundry






You will now see a message asking you to confirm you want to restore the iPhone and warning that it will be reverted to factory settings and all data erased. 
You will need to agree to Apple’s Terms. 
Your Mac will start to download the software (expect this to take a while).

						

							
6.
Wait while your Mac downloads the software


Mac downloading software in the background.

Foundry






Wait while the software update is downloaded and applied. Our’s estimated 20 minutes.
Your phone will exit Recovery mode after 15 minutes, but the Mac should continue to download the software update. 
You will need to put the iPhone back in Recovery mode to apply the update. 

						

							
7.
Your Mac will now apply the software update to the iPhone


The  Mac applies the software update. 

Foundry






Wait a few minutes while the software is applied.
Your iPhone will display the Apple logo and a progress bar, first while the update is applied and the again as it sets itself up. (Expect that to take a few minutes).

						

							
8.
Set up the iPhone as new

Foundry






Eventually the iPhone should restart with the Welcome screen if this process has worked.
You may see a screen that says “This iPhone is Locked to Owner” in various languages. If you know the password for the owner this shouldn’t be a problem. 
Now you can either set up your iPhone as new, or restore it from an iCloud backup. 
Tap on your country or region.
On the Quickly Set Up iPhone screen Click on Set Up Without Another Device (unless you have another iPhone you want to clone).
Connect to Wi-Fi.
Wait for your iPhone to activate. 
At this stage, if your iPhone is locked to a user you will need to add their email and password. You can also choose to unlock with the passcode. 
Now work through the various steps until you get to the Transfer Your Apps & Data screen and tap on From iCloud Backup (or Android). Check the date to make sure it’s the backup you want.
Log into your Apple ID and wait while your device signs in.
Now choose an iCloud backup from before you had problems with your iPhone. Click on Show more backups to find an older one if you don’t see it.
Wait while the Restore from iCloud takes place, which could take a while.

						

							
9.
What to do if you don’t know the password or pin

Apple






If the iPhone had Find My enabled on it and you don’t have the owners password or pin Activation Lock is triggered when you start the phone up after the restore.  
Unfortunately, you will need the owner’s Apple Account credentials to use the iPhone again after restoring.
However, you could try the steps in this article to help you unlock an Apple ID that’s locked or disabled.

title: Dark Cherry and More: Every iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Ultra Color Rumor
content:
We're likely about a month away from when Apple will launch new iPhone models, and color has been a major topic of discussion. There's going to be a dramatic new color for the iPhone 18 Pro and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, but Apple plans to play it safe with the foldable iPhone.


iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max

With the iPhone 17 Pro line, Apple introduced a bold new Cosmic Orange color. This year, Cosmic Orange is being retired for a shade that's darker and moodier.

Dark Cherry is the color Apple is rumored to be using, and it looks like a cross between red and purple.


Apple's colors always look different when lighting conditions change, which can lead to some confusion. At first, rumors described the color as a deep red.

also heard rumors about the possibility of burgundy, purple, and brown color options, with Apple set to choose one.



Macworld shared the exact Pantone colors Apple allegedly plans to use, describing the color as Dark Cherry for the first time. The site said the other three colors would include Silver, Dark Gray, and Light Blue. We used the Pantone shades to make a mockup.



Light Blue (Pantone 2121), resembling the current iPhone 17's Mist Blue

 
Dark Cherry (Pantone 6076), the headline new color

 
Dark Gray (Pantone 426C)

 
Silver (Pantone 427C), similar to the current generation


Dummy models soon surfaced showing similar colors, though with a bit more of a pink tone for the Dark Cherry shade.



The color Apple goes with will likely be close to the Pantone shade, with purple or red tones depending on the lighting. It's not quite burgundy because it trends closer to purple. It's redder than a true purple, but more violet than a dark red or maroon. It's more of a wine or a plum color, so if Dark Cherry is indeed the name of the color, it's a fitting one.

An alleged ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ SIM tray in Dark Cherry

We've had iPhones in Lavender, Pink, Deep Purple, (Product)RED, and Purple, but nothing like what Apple is planning for 2026.

There were only three color options for the ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ Max, but it looks like there will be four for the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models. Along with Silver and Dark Gray, there's a blue color.


Blue is a shade Apple has used for iPhone models multiple times in the past. The rumored blue is probably closest to the Sierra Blue color Apple used for the iPhone 13 Pro, but it's more saturated with less red and green to tone it down. Most of the blues Apple used in the past have been lighter or much darker, but this shade still won't feel as unique as the Dark Cherry color.

Uniform Back

The ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌ models have a two-tone design where the glass on the back is a noticeably lighter shade than the color of the aluminum frame. With the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models, the color difference between the frame and the glass panel at the back could be less pronounced.

minimize the color difference between the two components for a more unified appearance.
iPhone Ultra

While the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ and ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max will have two colors that offer options beyond the standard silver or gray, Apple doesn't plan to experiment with the foldable iPhone (which might be called the iPhone Ultra).

limited color palette. White has been mentioned multiple times, which probably means a white/silver type of shade, while rumors have been a little mixed on the second color (if there is one).

Macworld said in April that Apple would use silver and indigo, with the latter shade being similar to the Deep Blue color used for the ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌. In May, Weibo leaker Instant Digital said white was the only confirmed color, and in June, dummy models leaked alongside a rumor that the foldable iPhone might only be available in white.



that leaked in August suggest the foldable iPhone will come in silver/white and a dark blue shade that's almost black. Since the foldable iPhone is going to cost upwards of $2,000, it's not surprising Apple didn't want to make it in colors that might have narrower appeal.
Color Caveats

We're working with rumors and dummy models at this point. The colors that leak ahead of when a new iPhone launches are typically accurate, but lighting and material affect how color appears. Apple's devices often look far better than the dummy models and renderings.

were a duller shade than we actually got, plus nothing quite captured the two-tone look of the glass back and the frame. Ahead of the iPhone 16 Pro launch, there were rumors of a desert titanium shade. The mockups and dummy models were a darker, uglier brown than the soft, almost pink-toned gold shade Apple used.

It's unusual for the color rumors to be wrong, but it happens. Last year, rumors suggested there would be a black ‌iPhone 17 Pro‌, but it was a color Apple apparently dropped.
What About the iPhone 18?

The iPhone 18 isn't going to launch in the fall alongside the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models and the foldable iPhone. Apple's holding it until spring 2027, and since it's still months away, we haven't heard what its color options might be. With standard iPhones, Apple often debuts a range of colors.

There are five ‌iPhone 17‌ colors, including black, white, and three pastel shades in blue, lavender, and green. Apple tends to go back and forth between pastels and more saturated shades for the standard iPhone, so the 2027 ‌iPhone 18‌ could have brighter colors than the ones Apple used for the ‌iPhone 17‌ line.

iPhone Air 2, and we also don't know what colors Apple will use for those devices.
Launch Timing

Apple is expected to introduce the foldable iPhone and the ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ models at an iPhone event held the week of September 9. Pre-orders could start at the end of that same week, with a launch on September 18.

title: Apple Music to Label AI-Generated Songs
content:
Apple sent emails to its music industry partners about the upcoming launch of a Made With AI label that Apple will apply to AI-generated content (via The Hollywood Reporter).


Content tagged as being "materially generated using AI" will have a label visible to all Apple Music users.

announced Transparency Tags, a system that lets music creators disclose when AI has been used. Transparency Tags are available for artwork, track, composition (lyrics), and music video. Apple said at the time that the tags were optional, and it would defer to content providers to determine what qualifies as AI-generated.

In today's email, Apple says AI Transparency Tags are required in "any instance where AI was used to create a material portion of the content, including tracks that are AI platform generated." Apple said AI-platform-generated content is defined as "anything that is primarily derived from a generative AI service."

told Billboard that more than a third of monthly uploads to ‌Apple Music‌ are 100% AI-generated, but AI music accounted for less than 0.5% of actual listening. Schusser said Apple has an in-house system for detecting AI, but is still relying on content makers to disclose AI use.

title: ChatGPT Can Now Read and Send iMessages on Mac
content:

The Apple Messages plugin can be installed from the ChatGPT Plugins interface, and it is listed under Public. OpenAI suggests users try these prompts:

 	
Check my calendar and reply to [name] with a few times I'm free for dinner next week

 	
Suggest follow ups from yesterday in messages

 	
Find birthdays in @messages and add them to my calendar

 	
Find potential spam messages I can delete


RCS messages. Sending a message requires user approval by default, and OpenAI warns against granting persistent approval. For the Messages integration to work, ChatGPT needs Full Disk Access in System Settings, as well as access to contact names and automation tools.

Apple sued OpenAI over theft of trade secrets.

title: Apple Music's AI disclosure labels will soon be mandatory, rather than optional
content:
AI-generated content in the Apple Music app may get easier than ever to spot, as record labels and distributors will be required to label it as such later in 2026.


Apple Music's AI disclosure tags will soon become mandatory.
Back in March 2026, Apple introduced Transparency Tags for Apple Music. These are entirely optional disclosure labels, which were used to indicate that specific content was "materially generated" with the help of artificial intelligence.
At the time, Apple said it believed distributors should "take an active role in reporting when the content they deliver is created using AI," and that its AI-focused tags were "the first concrete step" in the process. So far, however, Apple hasn't forced labels or distributors to label AI-generated content, but that might soon change.

title: 2026 iPad mini guide: OLED, A19 Pro and price rumors
content:
Macworld





For those who need a premium small-screen tablet, the iPad mini is a popular choice. But should you buy one now, or should you wait to see what Apple has in store for the next model? 
Most buyers should wait – the next model is expected to bring meaningful upgrades. However, Apple isn’t expected to update the iPad mini until late 2026, and that launch date could slip further due to chip demand and wider supply constraints.
Here’s what the latest rumors say about the release date, key upgrades, and whether it’s worth waiting. 
2026 iPad mini: Rumored changes at a glance
A19 Pro (possibly A20 Pro)
Possible OLED display upgrade
Screen size could increase from 8.3-inch to 8.5- or 8.7-inches
More water-resistant design
Vibration-based speaker system
Price increase
Improved connectivity 


2026 iPad mini release date: When will the new iPad mini launch?
October 2026 is the reported timeframe
Apple has not officially announced a specific launch date for a new iPad mini. However, industry analysis and leaks suggest that a refresh is likely to occur before the end of 2026. In October 2025, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that a new iPad mini featuring an OLED screen is among the devices Apple is expected to launch before the end of 2026. In July 2026, Gurman reported that the OLED iPad mini is scheduled for an October 2026 release.
Several reports state that the macOS 26.7 release candidate includes references to the upcoming iPad mini. This confirms that a new iPad mini is planned, but the release date has yet to be established.
Several factors could influence the timing of its release and cause delays, though, including: 
Erratic release cycle: The iPad mini doesn’t follow a fixed update schedule and can go several years between refreshes. While some reports suggest Apple is aiming for a “sooner-than-later” update to bring it in line with newer chips, its history of two-year (or longer) gaps suggests another update isn’t imminent following the October 2024 model.
Component shortages: Apple’s plans may be affected by demand for the A18 Pro chip expected to power the device. This processor also powers the hugely popular MacBook Neo, which has led to reports that Apple could prioritise these chips for the Neo over the iPad mini. In addition, there are industry-wide supply pressures affecting RAM and other components which Apple CEO Tim Cook alluded to during the company’s first-quarter 2026 results announcement. 


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Performance and specs 
A19 Pro chip
C1X modem
N1 chip for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6
Since it hasn’t been updated in over a year, the next iPad mini is expected to receive several silicon upgrades. The current model features an A17 Pro chip, 8GB of RAM, and Apple Intelligence support. Most rumors suggest Apple will upgrade the device to the A19 Pro.
In August 2025, MacRumors reported that Apple code inadvertently revealed an A19 Pro-powered iPad mini, although the publication noted that the chip could also have been intended for the iPhone Air. Additional evidence emerged in December 2025, when Macworld reported seeing internal Apple code indicating that the entry-level iPad would launch with an A19 chip. Because Apple has traditionally equipped the iPad mini with a more powerful processor than the standard iPad, this lends further support to the A19 Pro rumor.
An A19 Pro would represent a substantial upgrade over the current A17 Pro. Users could expect faster on-device AI processing, improved gaming performance, and quicker photo and video editing. The A18 Pro, which powers the MacBook Neo, is often compared to the M1 chip and can rival the M3 in some single-core workloads. An A19 Pro-powered iPad mini would push the device even closer to iPad Air-level performance.
There are also reports that Apple could use the A20 Pro in the iPad mini instead. The likely chip may depend on launch timing. If the new iPad mini arrives before the iPhone 18 Pro, which is expected to debut the A20 Pro, the A19 Pro remains the most likely option. However, if the launch slips into late 2026 or beyond, an A20 Pro-equipped iPad mini becomes increasingly plausible.
A less ambitious upgrade to the A18 Pro remains possible. While the performance gains would be smaller, the chip still offers meaningful improvements over the A17 Pro thanks to architectural enhancements and a more powerful GPU configuration. In benchmarks, it would outperform the current model, though the difference would be less dramatic than with an A19 Pro or A20 Pro.
The popularity of the MacBook Neo could also influence Apple’s chip strategy. Reports suggest demand for the Neo has been strong enough to create pressure on A18 Pro supply, which could affect the availability of chips for other products.
Alongside processor upgrades, Apple is expected to bring its latest wireless technologies to the iPad mini. With the iPhone 17 lineup, Apple introduced the N1 chip, which supports Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. The company has already added the N1 to the M4 iPad Air and is expected to roll it out across the iPad lineup through 2026 and 2027, including the iPad mini. Cellular models are also expected to adopt Apple’s C1X modem.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Display
OLED display upgrade

The M4 iPad Pro’s OLED Display could make its way to the iPad mini next.

Mahmoud Itani / Foundry




The biggest display upgrade rumored for the next iPad mini is the adoption of OLED technology. Following Apple’s transition of the iPad Pro to OLED in 2024, multiple reports have suggested that the iPad mini will be the next iPad to make the switch. Ross Young of DSCC was first to claim, in a tweet in October 2024, that the next iPad mini would have a OLED. 
The current iPad mini, released in October 2024, still uses a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display, but industry sources, including Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, indicate a move to OLED is increasingly likely.
The transition from LCD to OLED would represent one of the most significant upgrades in the iPad mini’s history. Unlike LCD panels, which rely on a backlight, OLED displays illuminate each pixel individually. This allows pixels to switch off completely when displaying black content, resulting in deeper blacks, higher contrast ratios, and improved HDR performance.
Key benefits of OLED include:
Superior contrast and true blacks: Individual pixel control delivers inky blacks and virtually infinite contrast.
More vibrant colours: OLED panels typically offer wider colour gamuts and greater colour accuracy, producing richer and more immersive images.
Faster response times: Reduced motion blur and ghosting improve the experience when gaming or watching fast-moving content.
Better viewing angles: Colours and brightness remain consistent even when viewed from the side.
Improved efficiency: OLED can be more power-efficient when displaying darker content and allows for thinner display assemblies.
An OLED panel could also enable Apple to reduce bezel sizes, potentially increasing the display area slightly without significantly changing the tablet’s overall dimensions. Some reports suggest the screen could grow from 8.3 inches to around 8.5 inches as a result – more on that below.
While the iPad mini is unlikely to inherit premium display technologies such as ProMotion or the tandem OLED architecture used in the iPad Pro, the move to OLED would still deliver a noticeable improvement in visual quality, with richer blacks, better contrast, improved colour reproduction, and stronger HDR performance.
For users who prioritise display quality, an OLED iPad mini would address one of the most frequently cited limitations of the current model and bring the compact tablet much closer to the viewing experience offered by Apple’s premium devices.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Design
Same size, bigger screen possible
More water-resistant design rumored

Apple




The iPad mini has retained the same design since its major redesign in 2021, and the 2026 model is expected to keep that overall look. However, Apple could increase the display size slightly while maintaining the device’s current dimensions.
In December 2024, analysts at Display Supply Chain Consultants (DSCC) suggested in a supply chain analyst report that the next-generation iPad mini could feature an 8.5-inch display, up from the current model’s 8.3-inch panel. The reports indicated that the chassis size would remain unchanged, meaning Apple could achieve the larger screen through slimmer bezels rather than a larger body.
A larger display may also help the iPad mini maintain its place in Apple’s lineup as foldable devices arrive. Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone – often referred to as the iPhone Fold or iPhone Ultra – is expected to feature an inner display measuring between 7.6 and 7.8 inches with a 4:3 aspect ratio, putting it close to the iPad mini’s screen size. While still smaller than the iPad mini, such a device could appeal to some users who currently favour Apple’s smallest tablet. 
Another rumor gaining traction is that the new iPad mini will be more water-resistant. That rumor comes from Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, who in October 2025 claimed Apple was developing a next-generation iPad mini with a significantly more water-resistant chassis. 
The design changes could include: 
Redesigned casing with improved sealing around ports. 
A new speaker system that uses vibration-based audio technology to eliminate traditional speaker holes. 
There’s also a strong possibility of new colour options. Apple currently offers the iPad mini in Blue, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray, while the previous generation was available in Pink, Purple, Starlight, and Space Gray.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Cameras 
Little or no camera upgrade expected

Apple is not expected to upgrade the cameras in the next iPad mini.

Foundry




Apple’s iPads currently feature a 12MP Center Stage front-facing camera and a 12MP wide rear camera, and there are no credible reports suggesting major camera system upgrades for the next iPad mini. 
The most likely change concerns camera placement rather than camera hardware. Apple has moved the front-facing camera to the landscape edge on its latest iPad models, and the iPad mini could follow suit to improve the experience during video calls and FaceTime sessions when used with a keyboard or stand.
While the cameras themselves may remain unchanged, image quality could still benefit from improvements to the image signal processor and computational photography capabilities of a newer A-series chip.


						

							


2026 iPad mini: Price 
The iPad mini has had the same $499 price tag since its 2021 redesign. In 2026 we could see a price increase as a result of the OLED display upgrade. 
Component costs could also drive up the price. During Apple’s first quarter 2026 financial results announcement, CEO Tim Cook said that Apple is now “in a supply chase mode” due to industry-wide constraints. Thus, tariffs, the rising cost of RAM, and other increases in supply-chain costs could impact pricing for some higher-end storage options.
The price may remain the same though, with Apple wanting to keep the price of this niche product attractive.
